title: Introduction to New Features of Marvelous Designer 2025.1 - Custom Model Software Simulation
description: Thank you all for your continued support~! You can join the technical support group via private message to the backend.
transcript:
Self-designed model software simulation
Now software model simulation can be used to self-design virtual models,
including simple non-human shapes or virtual models without bones.
Now add an OBJ or FBX virtual model.
Here we add an OBJ file, then confirm the virtual model that is imported.
Please note that the virtual model you import cannot have a hole or a self-interference problem.
Go to the 3D window of the virtual model rendering type,
select the semi-transparent surface or display the frame to preview and check the potential problems.
Insert a costume that matches the size of the virtual model or create a costume for the virtual model.
Select the virtual model, then go to the property editor.
Under the surface settings, you can select the software model simulation.
Please remember to select CPU simulation, then turn on the simulation.
In this example, we will adjust the software model strength to 6500 and then check the final result.
In addition, you can also apply software model simulation to a simple structure object.
In this example, we are using a very simple object.
You can find it in the picture library, virtual model, fill-in model, and find it.
You need to select the virtual model display type.
Now we add the material outside of this model.
Create a rectangular board, place the board on the model.
Open the simulation, let it hang on the model.
Now we use the line sewing tool to sew the two ends of this fabric together.
In this example, we reduce the particle strength to 10,
then harden the board to make the simulation more stable and the effect more obvious.
Select the model, then open the software model simulation in the property editor.
Also remember to switch to CPU simulation, then turn on the simulation.
After opening the simulation, we will see the model under pressure transformation.
If your virtual model has an insertion part or a hole, a wrong spring will pop out.
In this example, this model has an insertion part.
This model also has a hole and insertion problem.
According to the conventional operation steps, this model is referred to as a virtual model.
After loading, we create a template to affect this model.
If you try to activate the software simulation function and open the simulation,
you will see the error prompt and point out the current file.
If you click OK, you will turn off the spring and disable the software model simulation.
Therefore, we again recommend that you open the semi-transparent display or open the display frame to check whether there is a problem affecting the software simulation.
If you want to use software model simulation for this model, you need to solve the problem first, then import the file into Marvelous Designer again.
That's all for this video. See you in the next video.
summary: ```markdown # Introduction to New Features of Marvelous Designer 2025.1 - Custom Model Software Simulation ## Self-Designed Model Software Simulation Now, software model simulation can be used to self-design virtual models, including simple non-human shapes or virtual models without bones. ## Importing Virtual Models To begin, add an OBJ or FBX virtual model. Here, we will add an OBJ file and then confirm the virtual model that is imported. > **Note:** The virtual model you import cannot have a hole or a self-interference problem. ## 3D Window and Rendering Type Go to the 3D window of the virtual model rendering type. You can select the semi-transparent surface or display the frame to preview and check for potential problems. ## Costume Matching Insert a costume that matches the size of the virtual model or create a costume specifically for the virtual model. Select the virtual model, then navigate to the property editor. ### Surface Settings Under the surface settings, you can select the software model simulation. Please remember to select CPU simulation and then turn on the simulation. In this example, we will adjust the software model strength to 6500 and then check the final result. ## Applying Software Model Simulation to Simple Structures In addition, you can also apply software model simulation to a simple structure object. In this example, we are using a very simple object that you can find in the picture library under virtual model fill-in models. ### Display Type Selection You need to select the virtual model display type. Now, we will add material to the outside of this model. Create a rectangular board and place it on the model. ## Simulation Setup Open the simulation to let the board hang on the model. We will use the line sewing tool to sew the two ends of this fabric together. ### Adjusting Particle Strength In this example, we reduce the particle strength to 10, then harden the board to make the simulation more stable and the effect more obvious. Select the model, then access the software model simulation in the property editor. Remember to switch to CPU simulation and then turn on the simulation. ## Observing Model Behavior After opening the simulation, we will see the model undergo pressure transformation. > **Important:** If your virtual model has an insertion part or a hole, a wrong spring will pop out. In this example, this model has an insertion part and also has a hole, leading to an insertion problem. ## Error Handling According to the conventional operation steps, this model is referred to as a virtual model. After loading, we create a template that affects this model. If you try to activate the software simulation function and open the simulation, you will see an error prompt indicating the current file. If you click OK, you will turn off the spring and disable the software model simulation. Therefore, we recommend again that you open the semi-transparent display or the display frame to check for any issues that might affect the software simulation. ## Final Steps If you want to use software model simulation for this model, you need to solve the problems first, then import the file into Marvelous Designer again. That's all for this video. See you in the next video. ```
